# Pimpampum

> A local, agent-first project manager for solopreneurs running a portfolio of
> products. One tiny background service gives every repository and every agent
> the same operational memory. The entire workflow is three calls. Specs and
> context stay readable Markdown; state stays in local SQLite on your own disk.

Pimpampum is for one person and the agents working for them. It has no sprints,
no estimates, no status columns and no meetings to keep them honest. It is MIT
licensed and the source is public.

## Install

No prompts, no root, no interactive steps. Safe for an agent to run unattended.

```
npm install --global pimpampum
pimpampum install
```

This creates one per-user background service and starts the local daemon at
login. Verify with `pimpampum status`. Requires Node.js 22 or newer.

On macOS 13 or newer with Apple Silicon there is also a signed menu-bar app in
GitHub Releases. On Omarchy there is a Quickshell widget that installs with the
plugin.

## Connect over MCP

The stdio bridge resolves its own credentials from the local data directory, so
an agent never handles a token.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pimpampum": {
      "command": "pimpampum-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

`pimpampum mcp` starts the same bridge through the main binary. MCP registry clients use that
route as `npx pimpampum mcp`, because `npx pimpampum` alone resolves to the CLI.

Hosts that speak streamable HTTP: `POST http://127.0.0.1:7337/mcp` with
`Authorization: Bearer <local-token>`. The token lives at
`<data-directory>/token` with mode 0600. `pimpampum config` reports the
effective data directory, base URL, MCP URL and stdio command, works offline,
and never prints the token itself.

## Or use the CLI, with no MCP

```
pimpampum commands
pimpampum tools
pimpampum call work_list --input '{"limit":20}'
```

Every command writes one `{"data": ...}` envelope to stdout and exits 0, or one
`{"error": ...}` envelope to stderr and exits non-zero. `help` is the single
exception and prints a text banner; `commands` returns the same catalog as JSON,
with every verb, its arguments, its options and its effect annotations. `--help`,
`-h`, `--version` and `-v` are accepted and exit 0.

Tool input comes from exactly one of `--input`, `--stdin` or `--input-file`.

Errors carry a stable code, a `retryable` boolean and a `suggestion`. When the
daemon does not answer, the code is `unavailable` and the suggestion names the
recovery command, so an agent never confuses a stopped service with a fault.

The named verbs (`work:start`, `work:complete`, `project:create`) wrap the same
tools and accept flags for everything the tools accept: `--lease-seconds`,
`--limit`, `--actor`, `--artifact` (repeatable) and `--artifacts` for labelled
references.

## The loop

- pim — `work_list` returns only the work that can be started right now.
- pam — `work_start` takes an expiring lease on exactly one Spec or leaf Task.
  Two agents can never grab the same job.
- pum — `work_complete` records a summary and artifact references, and releases
  the claim.

Renew a long claim with `work_renew`. Give it back untouched with
`work_release`. There is no fourth step.

## The model

Workspace (a product, anchored to one filesystem root) contains Projects. A
Project contains Specs. A Spec contains Tasks. A Task may contain one optional
level of Subtasks. That is the whole model.

A ready Spec with no open Tasks is claimable directly; once open Tasks exist,
only leaf Tasks are claimable. `doing` is derived from a live Claim and is never
persisted.

## Rules an agent must respect

- Claim before editing. A claim is an expiring lease, not a status field.
- Read only the Spec, Task and Context explicitly in scope. List tools return
  manifests and bounded reads, never whole bodies.
- Never create a project directly in `done`; call the completion operation.
- Never add subtasks while the parent task is claimed.
- Sync conflicts are preserved as visible conflicts. Explain the candidates;
  never resolve one autonomously.
- Errors carry stable codes. Do not flatten them.

## Sync between machines

Point it at a folder your provider already syncs — Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud
Drive, Syncthing, rclone. Pimpampum writes immutable JSON snapshots into
`Pimpampum/devices/<device>`; every computer keeps its own database, token and
claims. The live SQLite database must stay out of that folder.

```
pimpampum sync configure ~/Dropbox/Pimpampum --device laptop
```
